evidence.claim: Taiyo Yuden is presented in the candidate chunk as having explicit company evidence for an AI-server-targeted, high-capacitance embeddable MLCC.
Nitto Boseki is presented as a hypothesis requiring confirmation that it controls a dominant share of advanced T-glass supply for high-speed substrate materials.
Murata is presented as a reference leader for AI-server MLCC demand, with company and external evidence indicating server-related capacitor and power-supply-module growth.
TDK is presented as a reference product leader with explicit MLCC solutions for data-center and AI-server power systems, including PSU and intermediate bus converter use cases.

Vishay, Knowles, and Bel Fuse are presented as underfollowed or adjacent component hypotheses whose AI-server exposure requires verification through socket exposure, customer wins, backlog, or distributor evidence.
Constellium and Kaiser Aluminum are presented as possible alternative suppliers if an automotive aluminum rolling disruption causes customers to qualify non-Novelis capacity.
Centrus Energy is presented as a pure-play public-market exposure to U.S. enrichment and HALEU supply, a likely chokepoint if advanced reactor deployment accelerates.

memory_update.content: For New Hotspots Layer 3, prioritize underfollowed candidates only when the hidden supply-chain signal is both material and testable; do not over-rank obscure names with generic component exposure.

Next step for AI-server MLCC/passives cluster: verify Taiyo Yuden, Murata, TDK, Vishay, Knowles, and Bel Fuse through primary filings, product datasheets, distributor inventory/backlog, customer qualification commentary, and server/accelerator teardown evidence.
Next step for Nitto Boseki: confirm or falsify the advanced T-glass dominance claim using filings, capacity disclosures, substrate-material customer references, and credible industry sources.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the AI-server MLCC product has design wins with major accelerator or server platforms and whether capacity is material to consolidated revenue.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source confirmation from company filings, product disclosures, customer qualification commentary, distributor checks, or teardown evidence showing that AI-server MLCC exposure is material rather than merely product-line optionality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Highest-priority Serenity candidate in this chunk because it sits directly in the AI-server passive-component chain through high-end MLCCs, has explicit company-level product evidence in the candidate record, and remains less crowded than Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, optical names, or semiconductor leaders. The thesis is also falsifiable through AI-server design wins, capacity allocation, product mix, and revenue contribution.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: More obscure to U.S. investors than global passive-component leaders and often screened as a generic Japanese electronics supplier rather than as a possible AI-server power-density bottleneck beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm through company filings, capacity-expansion disclosures, substrate customer references, and industry sources whether Nitto Boseki is the specific public company controlling roughly 90% of global T-glass supply.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The strongest bottleneck claim is still a hypothesis in the provided candidate record. It needs direct corroboration from primary filings, customer qualification data, substrate supplier disclosures, or credible industry sources before it can outrank better-evidenced candidates.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potentially one of the most valuable chokepoint hypotheses in the chunk if Nitto Boseki is confirmed as the dominant supplier of advanced T-glass or similar high-speed substrate glass-fiber material. The suspected bottleneck has strong Serenity characteristics: specialized chemistry, qualification cycles, limited substitutes, and hidden exposure one layer below AI accelerators and advanced packages.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Known in Japanese electronic-materials circles but much less visible in broad AI baskets, which usually concentrate on GPUs, HBM, optics, networking, and semiconductor equipment.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI/data-center MLCC revenue growth is driven by mix and ASP rather than only unit volume; watch backlog, price increases, and capacity-expansion timing.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level detail showing that AI/data-center MLCC exposure is large enough to affect consolidated earnings and that any scarcity translates into pricing power rather than just volume growth.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Best reference leader for validating the AI-server MLCC bottleneck because the provided candidate record indicates company and external evidence for server-related capacitor and power-supply-module growth. It helps define product requirements, demand durability, pricing, and capacity behavior for smaller or less-followed peers.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not truly underfollowed within Japan or electronics, but it is still less central than GPUs, HBM, optics, and AI power-grid names in U.S.-centric AI infrastructure narratives.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether TDK is winning high-end decoupling sockets close to GPUs/accelerators, or mainly PSU/IBC sockets with different margin and scarcity characteristics.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need application-level evidence distinguishing scarce, high-margin accelerator-board sockets from broader power-supply or passive-component demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Useful reference comp for data-center and AI-server power-system components, especially MLCCs, inductors, PSU components, and intermediate bus converter use cases. It is less of a pure discovery name but valuable for mapping where high-end passive and power-delivery constraints may appear.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not a small-cap or obscure discovery candidate, but often less central than GPUs, HBM, networking, and power-infrastructure names in AI-infrastructure narratives.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Look for AI-server or data-center socket exposure in high-current inductors, ceramic MLCCs, polymer/tantalum capacitors, current-sense resistors, or distributor backlog rather than relying on generic passive-component exposure.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that AI-server or data-center orders are material and differentiated, not simply part of broad cyclical component demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong underfollowed second-order candidate because Vishay is publicly listed, mid-cap, and exposed to capacitors, inductors, resistors, discrete semiconductors, and board-level power components that could benefit from AI-server power-density growth. The ranking is held back by weak direct evidence for AI-server socket exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually categorized as a cyclical discrete/passive component manufacturer rather than an AI-server bottleneck name; AI exposure may be hidden inside broad industrial, computing, distributor, and power-electronics channels.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm current DOE procurement awards, HALEU production scale, licensing status, funding cadence, and whether revenue conversion is material versus policy-option value.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current primary-source confirmation of DOE awards, production scale, revenue timing, and licensing milestones. The thesis may be more policy-option value than near-term operating leverage.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Ranks high on bottleneck purity because U.S. uranium enrichment and HALEU supply are regulated, scarce, and potentially critical for advanced reactor deployment. It is less aligned with the AI-server passive-component sub-theme but still fits the broader New Hotspots funnel as a regulated-asset chokepoint.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Known among nuclear specialists but still narrow compared with broad AI and power-infrastructure baskets; exposure is unusually pure but dependent on policy, procurement, licensing, and funding milestones.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether Knowles' MLCC and capacitor products are qualified into AI servers, data-center power systems, optical networking, accelerator boards, or power-delivery modules rather than only defense/industrial/medical niches.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need customer, product, or distributor evidence showing material exposure to AI servers, optical networking, or data-center power systems.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Interesting adjacent specialty-components candidate because AI-server density could raise the value of high-reliability capacitors, EMI filtering, specialty MLCCs, and board-space optimization. However, the AI-server linkage is currently weaker than for Taiyo Yuden or Murata.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often associated with microphones, medtech, RF filters, or specialty components rather than AI-server board-level power decoupling.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether AI-server racks, accelerator servers, or hyperscale data-center customers are materially driving orders for Bel's magnetic, inductor, power-shelf, or high-efficiency power products.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct data-center or hyperscale customer evidence and proof that demand is scarce or margin-accretive rather than generic component-cycle recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potentially attractive underfollowed AI-server power-density adjacency through magnetics, inductive components, protection products, power supplies, and connectivity. It is testable via backlog, customer commentary, and data-center product wins, but the current evidence is inferential.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: More likely to be classified as a small electronic-components or power/connectivity supplier than as an AI infrastructure component beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check whether automakers redirected volumes from Novelis to Constellium, whether qualification cycles created durable share shift, and whether pricing/mix improved after the Oswego outage.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need hard evidence of customer volume transfers, qualification wins, contract repricing, or margin uplift tied to the disruption rather than normal aluminum-cycle dynamics.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potential beneficiary if an automotive aluminum rolling disruption forces customers to qualify alternative suppliers. It is underfollowed as a supply-chain rerouting candidate, but the linkage depends on specific customer qualification, capacity availability, and mix improvement.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually screened as a cyclical aluminum processor rather than as a bottleneck beneficiary from an auto supply-chain outage.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify automotive body sheet capability, customer qualification status, any incremental spot or contract volumes after the Novelis Oswego disruption, and margin impact.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation that Kaiser has relevant automotive body sheet capability and qualified customer relationships that can absorb redirected demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Speculative but testable alternative-supplier thesis if automotive or industrial customers seek non-Novelis aluminum rolling capacity after a supply disruption. The small-cap profile gives discovery potential, but the product fit and customer qualification evidence remain uncertain.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Investor narrative usually focuses on aluminum prices or aerospace cycles, not possible customer qualification changes caused by a competitor outage.

summary: Layer 3 ranking for the provided candidate chunk prioritizes obscure, testable supply-chain chokepoints over popular reference leaders. Highest priority goes to candidates with explicit AI-server or regulated bottleneck exposure, plausible supplier scarcity, and a clear evidence path. Taiyo Yuden ranks first because it combines underfollowed AI-server MLCC exposure, direct component relevance, and a verifiable design-win/capacity question. Nitto Boseki ranks second as a high-upside advanced substrate-material bottleneck hypothesis, but remains evidence-gated. Murata and TDK are retained as reference leaders rather than alpha-discovery names. Vishay, Knowles, Bel Fuse, Constellium, Kaiser Aluminum, and Centrus remain useful follow-up candidates but require sharper proof that the suspected chokepoint is material to revenue, margins, or backlog.
